points.description: Observes that the circumcircle of P_A P_B P_C is the reflection of the circumcircle of ABC across P, so it has the same radius R and center 2P−O (O = circumcenter of ABC).

Argues that two distinct equal circles meet in exactly one point only when externally tangent (center distance 2R), giving |PO| = R; notes P = O gives identical circles (not good). So the locus is the circle of radius R centered at O.
Computes the circumradius R = abc/(4K) = 13·14·15/(4·84) = 65/8 (area K = 84 from Heron).

rubric.notes: Full mark only if all steps are valid and the final answer 4225π/64 is correct; any wrong step or wrong final answer earns 0. Equivalent wording and alternative valid methods are accepted.
rubric.answer_key: Reflected circle has same radius R and center 2P−O. Equal circles touch at exactly one point iff centers are 2R apart, so |PO| = R. Locus is a circle of radius R about O. R = (13·14·15)/(4·84) = 65/8. Area = π(65/8)² = 4225π/64.
